question.leadin: This emperor killed his mother Agrippina the Younger and his first wife Octavia and forced Seneca the Younger to commit suicide for his alleged involvement in the Pisonian Conspiracy.
question.text: Name this Roman emperor who was the first emperor to commit suicide, after learning that he had been sentenced to death in absentia.
question.answerHtml: Nero [accept Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, but do NOT accept Claudius, Caesar, Augustus, or Germanicus alone]
question.clue: This emperor constructed the Domus Aurea and his death marked the beginning of the Year of the Four Emperors.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the history of the Roman Republic.
swap.text: The government of the early Roman Republic was dominated by these upper-class citizens, who are often contrasted with the working-class plebeians [pleh-BEE-unz].
swap.clue: They were identified by shoes of red leather, an iron ring, and a broad purple stripe worn down the right side of their tunics.

question.leadin: To complete this siege, attacking forces built a wall around a hilltop fort, then built a wall around themselves to protect from a reinforcing army.
question.text: Name this 52 BCE siege of a hilltop fort commanded by Vercingetorix, whose surrender essentially guaranteed the fall of Gaul.
question.clue: A group of Mandubii civilians became trapped between the two sides of this battle and were left to starve.

swap.text: The grandest examples of gladiatorial combat took place in this Roman arena, the largest amphitheater ever built.
swap.clue: While not for getting sick, this location's vomitorium allowed for the rapid entrance and exits of spectators to various parts of it.

question.text: In 8 B.C. Augustus assumed this office whose duties included overseeing the counting of the people. This official could also remove names from the senator list; overseeing publications is an act such officials still do today.
question.clue: Only former consuls could be named to this powerful office, which determined eligibility for voting and oversaw public morals laws.

swap.leadin: Lars Porsena ruled this civilization's city of Clusium.
swap.text: Name this ancient Italian civilization whose people referred to themselves as the Rasenna and lived on the coast of the Tyrrhenian Sea.
swap.clue: These people were organized into the Dodecapoli, twelve cities that formed their namesake league.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the rise of Rome.
question.text: Rome's first king and legendary founder was this man. This man murdered his twin brother, Remus.
question.clue: Fighting between factions loyal to him and factions loyal to Tatius eventually led to Numa Pompilius being crowned as this man's successor.

swap.text: Lars Porcena was ostensibly helping this man regain his control of Rome. This man, supposedly the son of an earlier king with a similar name, lost power after his son raped Lucretia.
swap.answerHtml: Tarquin the Proud [accept Lucius Tarquinius Superbus; prompt on Tarquinius; do not accept "Lucius Tarquinius Priscus]
swap.clue: This last king of Rome was legendarily deposed and exiled after his son Sextus raped Lucretia, the wife of Lucius Collatinus.

question.text: Piux IX installed a statue of this first pope in his namesake basilica in the Vatican. As an apostle this man denied Jesus three times.
question.clue: This first Pope was one of the Twelve Apostles. He also names a Basilica in the Vatican.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about people who may have come from Lydia or Umbria.
swap.text: This Italian civilization, which was eventually absorbed by the Romans, had no centralized government. Instead, it was comprised of a loose Confederation of cities like Clusium and Veii.
swap.clue: The names of gods in this language are on a sheep liver-shaped bronze artifact used for haruspicy found at Piacenza.

question.leadin: During times of crisis, these people were often scapegoated and buried alive near the Colline Gate.
question.text: Name these Roman priestesses who served 30-year terms maintaining the city's sacred fire.
question.clue: These people oversaw rites during the Bona Dea festival.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Roman occupation of Britain.
swap.text: As governor of Britannia, this Roman general subdued the Caledonians and Ordovices, winning the battle of Mons Graupius in Scotland. Father-in-law of Tacitus, he was recalled by Domitian, but not before he circumnavigated Britain.
swap.clue: He served under Salvius Titianus after being appointed quaestor in Asia and after he shared a battle tent with his military tutor Suetonius Paulinus.

question.leadin: Viriathus led a rebellion that Polybius called the "fiery war" in this region, where velites ("WAY-lee-tace") units failed to counter weapons like the pilum ("PEE-loom") and falcata in the Numantine War.
question.text: Identify this region that contained the mysterious Tartessos civilization. After Sulla's civil war, Quintus Sertorius led a revolt in this region, where "New Carthage" controlled rich silver mines before the Battle of Ilipa ("ILL-ipp-uh").
question.answerHtml: Hispania [accept Iberia or Iberian peninsula; accept Spain or España; accept Portugal; accept Catalonia or Catalunya; accept Hispania Baetica or Hispania Tarraconensis or Hispania Citerior or Hispania Ulterior; accept Lusitania or Lusitanian War; accept Andalusia or Andalucía; accept Murcia] (“New Carthage” is Cartagena.)
question.clue: Hasdrubal Gisco lost to a "reverse Cannae" at Ilipa ("ILL-ih-puh") in this region, which was later the location of the Numantine War.

swap.text: As part of his reunification of the Roman Empire, Aurelian was forced to abandon this Roman province north of the Danube, which had been established by Trajan after conquering a namesake tribe under King Decebalus.
swap.answerHtml: Dacia [or Roman Dacia or Dacia Traiana or Dacia Felix; accept Dacians]
swap.clue: Soldiers of this region used the sickle-like falx during a war in which a bridge near the Iron Gates was built by Apollodorus.

question.text: This king of Clusium had his invasion of Rome repelled by the heroic actions of Horatius Cocles on the Pons Sublicius, as immortalised in a poem by T. B. Macaulay.
question.clue: This figure was saved from death when a would-be assassin mistook his scribe for him, and that assassin thrust his right hand into a fire in an act of defiance against this figure.

swap.text: This queen of the Iceni revolted against Nero after her husband Prasutagus' will was ignored, and her daughters were raped. Her forces decisively defeated the 9th Legion but lost the Battle of Watling Street.
swap.clue: This person's popularity as a patriotic symbol in Victorian Britain was influenced by the theory that her name comes from a root meaning "victory" in Celtic.

question.leadin: You are a sailor in the Roman navy.
question.text: Because you are inexperienced at seaborne combat, you are grateful for the invention of this device, a large hinged bridge which is slammed down on opposing ships to turn sea battles into hand-to-hand combat.
question.clue: This device that allowed soldiers to board enemy ships after a bridge with a spike on the bottom was lowered onto the enemy's hull.

swap.text: Name this speech which was written to acquit its title politician of the murder of Clodius.
swap.clue: This defense oration which becamse known in published form, composed for the Optimate rival of Julius Caesar, who was charged with murder following an incident at Bovillae.

question.text: The First Punic War was sparked by this group of Italian mercenaries, who requested Carthaginian aid after losing to Hieron II, but switched to the Roman side when the Carthaginian army arrived.
question.clue: Pyrrhus was also opposed by this band of mercenaries hired by Agathocles, the Tyrant of Syracuse. They later sided with Rome against Syracuse and Carthage during the First Punic War.

swap.text: Per Strabo, either this man's father or son led an expedition to find the sources of tin in the 1st century BCE. This man established a corrupt private force whose function Augustus later replaced with the vigiles.
